got_right: Eleven interventions were randomised against one shared control in a registered design (AsPredicted #151,281), with both Lin-adjusted and unadjusted models. This exposed that the Guide (+4.7) and Mindfulness (−3.9) adjusted effects vanish in raw means (+0.6, +0.2).
Automated Flagging is the one result that survives both specifications: +4.4 points adjusted (p=0.004) and +3.2 unadjusted (p=0.028).
Splitting accuracy into AI-post and real-post detection (H5/H6) separates better discernment from a shift in response bias, which total accuracy hides.
Reporting the pooled random-effects estimate (+1.0 point, CI [−0.3, 2.4]) and the uncorrected test count (44 registered, 22 post hoc) keeps the overall null honest.

why_it_did_not_land.detail: The control group has only 181 respondents and several arms have under 100. Most arms cannot detect effects below about 3.5 to 5 points, so the 1 to 2 point effects seen are undetectable.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: H1 MDEs: 0.032 (AI Accuracy Nudge) to 0.052 (Inoculation, Infographic 2); observed non-significant arms are mostly 0.01 to 0.02.

why_it_did_not_land.detail: About 44 uncorrected arm tests, and the nominal wins (Guide, Mindfulness, Breathing on attitudes) depend on the covariate model. They are not credible effects.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: H1 Guide p=0.043 adjusted vs 0.671 unadjusted; H2 Breathing −0.54 adjusted vs −0.04 in H2a.

why_it_did_not_land.detail: Total accuracy mixes sensitivity and bias. Arms raising AI-post detection may just make people say 'AI' more often, and no signal-detection measure separates the two.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: H5 Breathing +9.1 and Nudge +6.6 on AI posts, with H6 real-post estimates of −4.8 and −1.8 and no total-accuracy gain (+1.5, +2.0).

why_it_did_not_land.detail: Arms are unbalanced and bundle different mechanisms (labels, priming, education). Outcomes are measured immediately after a one-off exposure, so persistence and real behaviour are untested.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: Arm n from 78 to 333; the design lists 11 heterogeneous arms with a single post-exposure feed.

debates.label: Individual-level vs system-level fixes
debates.position_a: Brief individual-level interventions can improve people's handling of misinformation.
debates.position_b: Individual-level (i-frame) interventions are weak and distract from structural, system-level remedies.
debates.what_this_study_says: It leans toward b. Only platform-supplied labels (Automated Flagging, +4.4) moved accuracy. User-side education and mindfulness did nothing reliable. The arms are too heterogeneous and underpowered to settle it.

briefs.title: Discernment vs response bias in AI labels
briefs.question: Does Automated Flagging improve true discernment (d') or only shift willingness to answer 'AI'?
briefs.why_this_fixes_the_failure: Fixes measurement: computes sensitivity and criterion from AI and real post responses, and adds confidence ratings.
briefs.design_sketch: Arms: control, Automated Flagging, and Automated Flagging with a stated label error rate (e.g. 80% accurate). Each respondent judges 24 posts, half AI-generated, with a per-item confidence rating. Outcomes are d' and criterion, plus a sharing intention. Recruit a US online panel.

power_target.basis: Observed Automated Flagging effect 0.032 to 0.044 on total accuracy; H1 MDE at n=127/181 was 0.042; n=400/arm gives about 0.028 for SD 0.13.

briefs.title: Platform labels vs user training head to head
briefs.question: Do system-supplied cues outperform individual-level training on AI detection, as the s-frame view implies?
briefs.why_this_fixes_the_failure: Fixes design and power: contrasts only the best-supported system arm with the best user-side arm in a focused comparison.
briefs.design_sketch: Four arms: control, Automated Flagging, AI Literacy Guide, and both combined. Outcomes are accuracy on AI and real posts, assessed immediately and again after 1 week. Pre-register the contrast labels vs guide and test the additive combination.

power_target.basis: Observed Guide-vs-control raw difference 0.006 and adjusted 0.047; size to detect a 0.03 label-vs-guide gap (H1 SD about 0.13).

briefs.title: Label effect by label reliability and prior AI skill
briefs.question: Does the Automated Flagging benefit hold when labels are imperfect and across respondents with different AI familiarity?
briefs.why_this_fixes_the_failure: Fixes the sample and missing-moderator causes by testing where the one robust effect holds.
briefs.design_sketch: Randomise label reliability (95% vs 70% accurate) crossed with a control, using video and image stimuli. Stratify recruitment by the AI-familiarity scale (ai_scale). Outcome is accuracy on both AI and real posts.
briefs.moderator_or_condition: Label reliability and AI familiarity (ai_scale), with stimulus type (image vs video)

power_target.basis: Observed Automated Flagging +0.032 raw; n=350/arm gives MDE about 0.03 at SD 0.13.

verdict: A follow-up is worth running, but narrowly. The only robust result is Automated Flagging (+3.2 to +4.4 points), while the other nominal effects vanish without covariates. Run the advance_design brief first: it tests whether the label effect is real discernment or a shift toward answering 'AI', and it is sized to the observed effect. The head-to-head debate brief should follow. The literature retrieved is thin on AI-media detection, so the i-frame vs s-frame debate rests on one contesting source (Chater & Loewenstein) and should be treated as framing, not established disagreement.
